lines.dialogue: Kids! Breakfast!
What's with the workout clothes? Kids!!!
Eight.
I think about that every single day. BREAKFAST!!!
Haley, you're not wearing that skirt.
It's too short. People can tell you're a girl, you don't have to prove it to them.
It's in our night stan-- I don't know -- find it!

Raising kids is like building a car. You only have so much time to make sure the steering works and the brakes stop and the engine is dependable before you send it out on the road, and if you get one little rivet wrong, it will drive off a cliff and explode.
Who's coming over anyway?
Him?
Okay, why don't you guys go outside for a little bit?
So, who is this boy?
Honey, it's the first time you're having a boy over, I'm bound to be a little surprised, but I'm not going to embarrass you.
Honey, relax.
Are you okay?
What did I tell you would happen if you bought him a gun?
Are you insane, you're going to shoot him?! He's got a birthday party.
He can't show up with a big hideous welt. You can shoot him later. He'll be home at two.
No, he's got a soccer game at three. We've got to leave for that dinner at five. You can shoot him at four- fifteen.
Shoot Luke.
Hello, you must be Dylan.
Hang on. How old are you, Dylan?
Oh. That's, um...
Phil, Dylan's here and he's seventeen.
Honey?
Should I call the doctor?
Alex, leave your sister alone.
You need to respect their privacy. What are they doing up there?
with this) Oh. Oh. Well, good. So, I'm making a cake for tonight, want to help me?
Sure, sweetie.
Wow, I remember when you used to trip over this thing.
What?
Alex, Haley is not getting pregnant.
panic) But there's no point in saying if. If is what you say when things can happen and this can't happen. I can't believe I have to prove this to you.
What am I doing? Seeing if you guys need anything, okay?

Knock? You knock when you think people are doing something private, which you aren't, obviously, why would you be? Although I think we all read that study this week saying thirty-nine-percent of sixteen-year- olds have had sexual intercourse. And as long as we're talking, what is with the coffee all the time? Huh? Whatever happened to ice cream? And all the texting and your cell phones glued to your hands, like you're little business-people. Doesn't anyone want to run around and ride bikes and be kids anymore?
So did you guys need anything?
Hey!
Don't thank me, just open it. Dad was parking right behind us.
Dad!
That's nothing. She had her first boy over today, I lost it in front of them and then Phil shot him.
Phil! That's how she says "Phil".
What?!
She's yours?!
Let me help.
How could you not say something?

I love how you see me as some huge busybody. takes over changing the diaper) I mean, yes, it's a huge responsibility, it's gonna put a lot of pressure on you two that you might not be able to handle. What did Mom say?
So what do you know about her parents?
Oh, God. Well, she's gorgeous.
What?

Oh honey, don't be ridiculous. You're her parents. Of course she'll be ashamed of you. My kids are mortified by me. Which is pretty ironic considering Haley dresses like a hooker, Alex dresses like a lesbian and...
...Luke can barely get his shoes on the right feet. And tell me you're not horrified by Dad and that Huggy Bear outfit that Charo out there bought for him.
The point is, Lily is the luckiest little girl in the world, getting you two. So stop worrying.
Come on, we're all together. Let's go out there and enjoy this.
Oh, hi.
This is my son Luke and my husband Phil. And this is...
Right. I’m sorry. Desiree just moved in down the street.
Phil, that’s creepy.
Well, nice to see you.
We are never having her over. I heard she slept with two dads at the school already.
Phil, you’re kind of hurting me.
Phil, what are you do--
I thought you were taking out the garbage.
Phil.
Did you ring the bell?
Tell her I said hi.
I was being --
Gee, maybe teenaged boys don’t like hanging out with their girlfriends’ dads.
I thought you were all about keeping it real.
You haven’t exactly taken it to the next level with my dad.
We’ve been married sixteen years and you still walk on eggshells around him.
Luke’ll love that. He’s in the back yard.
I don’t think so, but thanks.
Don’t you say hi to Gloria and Manny?
No. You’re wearing a dress.
It’s not going to kill you to look like a girl for one evening.
This is not up for discussion. Just borrow one of Haley’s again.
What?
Oh, why does he --
Luke! Pants!
That’s a nice offer, but it’s not really Alex’s thing.
Yes, your thing is to provoke, just like your sister’s thing is to never come out of her room. And your brother’s thing is... visible to the Hendersons. Luke! Put ‘em on!
No, I just put ‘em in the oven.
Sure. So how are you and Luke getting along?
What do you mean?
Oh, it’s nothing. Just dealing with some Alex stuff. You know, kids.
Alex and I can’t just disagree. She has to turn everything into a fight.
Yeah, but I was never hostile. Like this whole dress thing. I never had that trouble with Haley.
For one afternoon.
You know, Manny, sometimes I forget you’re only ten-years-old.
Hello? Olives? Well... yeah, I guess so...
Alex, I’ve been thinking about it, and it’s not the end of the world if you don’t wear a dress to the wedding.
What happened?
Will somebody tell me what happened?
Like when you ran over his foot?
You went out of your way. We could all see the tire marks on the lawn --
I’ve seen you thread the needle a million times. You never miss.
Why don’t you admit it. You never liked Phil. And put that down. You do not get a cookie.
Maybe he tries too hard because you never make any kind of effort. In sixteen years, have you ever once told him you liked him?
You haven’t said it in any words! You know how that makes me feel?
Okay, Dad, thanks for bringing Phil home. I found one of your little flaps in his hair.

lines.dialogue: Forty dollars?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: What book?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Do you have any idea what a bad liar you are?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Well, that’s a first. Inside out and backwards. At least it’s not zipped into your -- oop, there it is.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Pork Surgeon.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: ...okay, thanks. We’ll be right there.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Luke got in a fight at school.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: He’s fine, but they want us to come down there. Where are you?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Which house?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: I’ll bet you anything it was that Durkas kid.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: He probably jumped on Luke and Luke fought back. The kid’s a menace.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Shh, his parents are probably right inside.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: What are you doing here? GLORIA The same thing you’re doing here.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: What?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: So, what happened? GLORIA Yes, what happened? MR. BALABAN Well, apparently there was some name calling and shoving on the playground. By the time a teacher separated them, Luke was sitting on Manny’s chest.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: He’s our son.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: And I’m his daughter. MR. BALABAN So, you’re...

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Is that what the fight was about?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: You heard how she said that -- “Jess.” She thought Luke was the weird one.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: He wears aftershave and dresses like a count -- does she even see that?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: She’s the one with the problem, not me. PHIL Okay, okay. I just hate to see my two girls not getting along. CLAIRE How is she your girl? JAY She’s my daughter, you’re my wife. Let’s remember what’s important here: there’s a football game on. PHIL So, you okay?

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Jess...

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: No, more “juh” sound.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Nope, you can’t do it.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: Let me guess, the game’s on.

lines.scene: INT. JAY & GLORIA'S HOUSE - HALLWAY/MASTER BEDROOM
lines.dialogue: No. PHIL I... didn’t respond because this shouldn’t be about me, it should be about you two. Talking. Alone. CLAIRE I don’t know what to say except that I’m really sorry. GLORIA Okay. Just let me ask you one thing, and it’s okay if the answer is no. Are you happy I married your father? CLAIRE Happy? GLORIA I knew it. CLAIRE I’m still getting used to it, that’s all. You don’t expect to wake up one day with a new mom that looks like she
Okay, your brother’s lunch is packed. You’re buying your own lunch. Where’s Alex?
Wow, school hasn’t even started and you’re already behind.
Getting everybody out the door in the morning is tough -- especially on the first day of school.
I get up at six.
This is why we suggested the violin.
Phil, put on some pants.
Which is a whole other discussion. Haley, don’t forget, the driving instructor is picking you up from school.
Haley just got her learner’s permit.
It makes you realize we’re all hanging by a thread.
Merge... merge... Merge! Merge! MERGE!
Hello.
We usually just gave them time-outs.
Relax. It happens. Luke used to hit his head all the time and he’s fine.
Yeah. I’ve been meaning to get to it for a while.
I thought you had an open house this morning.
I’m good. I’m kind of looking forward to a quiet day. I’ll probably go for a run a little later, but that’s about it.
You don’t have to do that.
The thing is I kind of like to run alone. Besides, I run pretty fast.
Um... I’m just not sure you’ll be able to keep up.
No.
You barely seem able to keep up with this conversation.
I know. But I run everyday.
No. I think I can run much, much faster.
I just want to read.
Phil, let it go. I’m faster than you.
You seriously want to race me? I ran a half-marathon last year.
You know what? You’re right -- we do have to do this. I’ll go get changed.
Fine. This afternoon.
I didn’t say anything.
I don’t know.
Are you?
Go.
Yes.

I run five miles a day. I have a resting heart rate of forty-eight. I would never lose a two mile race to Johnny Ski Pole. But after seeing the look on Phil’s face when the kids came home from school and then seeing that shirt, I realized something. The first day of school is a big adjustment for all of us, but it’s especially hard on Phil.
Oh my God. Phil!
Did I lose the race to cheer him up? Maybe.
We do strange things for our loved ones. Lie to them, lie for them.
There might be some bumps along the way, but we never stop wanting the best for them. And that’s what makes it such a tough job...
...And kind of the best job in the world.
What was that for?
I love you, too.
I don’t know. I’m kinda gross. I don’t feel like getting all dressed now.
Huh. That sounds pretty good, actually. I can read my book.
About.
The greatest.
But the best at something? Uh, well, let’s think...
And Haley...
Gorgeous.
Sweet, sweet Luke.
Looks like Dad wants this even more than Manny does.
What are you babbling about? MITCHELL Oh, so now I’m a babbler. CLAIRE Did I do something wrong? MITCHELL What? No. I’m just happy for Manny. Everything isn’t always about Claire.
What? Alex.
Alex, be nice. Haley, stop being such an easy target.
What are you guys doing?
Baseball. Why not? Someone’s gotta play it, right?

I see why you ruled out math. CLAIRE Would I like Luke to be successful? Of course. But unlike my husband, I don’t think a parent can force it. You just have to have faith that your kid’s gonna find his own way. Besides, Luke’s already the best at one thing... being my son. I promise that sounded a lot less lame in my head.
That’s not exactly how I remember it.
At what?
Oh my God, that’s amazing!
Wait a minute, why is your iPod in your mouth?
Alex!
Hey, you made out with him, too.
Look, I was bigger than you. I was afraid that you couldn’t lift me. You dropped me a lot at practice. I didn’t want to see you humiliated in front of everyone.
Now can you please just forgive me and move on?
Well, a little, but we all have our stuff. I’m just glad you finally got it out of your -- Are you trying to lift me?
And you thought the path to Dad’s approval was through figure skating? I’m pretty sure his proudest moment came when you finally hung up the fire red unitard.
No. Believe it or not I always felt bad that I quit. I know how much you loved skating.
What?
I can take it.
Wow. That is... a little gay.
Get up.
Just don’t drop me.
